Added 2026-07-19 ([specialist]), closing a zero-fact income-viability gap across all five Mexico locations (country-scope, applies to all). 315.04 MXN/day general zone, 440.87 MXN/day Northern Border Free Zone; 13% YoY increase (6.5% fixed adjustment + MXN 17.01 Independent Recovery Amount/MIR), CONASAMI 2026 DOF publication. Added 2026-07-19 ([specialist]). Pilot program registering delivery/rideshare gig workers with the public health-insurance system (IMSS) concluded Dec 2025; mandatory enrollment nationwide from Jan 1, 2026. Net-income exclusion factors vary by vehicle type: up to 48% (cars), 32% (motorcycles), 3% (non-motorized). Relevant context if a small-group arrival considers local gig income as a supplement — now a real, registered, IMSS-linked system, not an informal cash economy

fact_label: Remote work on tourist (FMM) status — legal gray area, not aggressively enforced
value_raw: Legally ambiguous (not explicitly authorized under tourist status)
notes: Added 2026-07-19 ([specialist]). Mexican law distinguishes tourism from 'lucrative activities'; remote work for a foreign employer isn't explicitly authorized under FMM tourist status but has historically not been aggressively enforced against — probably the single most common quiet remote-work-on-tourist-status arrangement of any country in this project. Real, current tightening trend: officer discretion increasingly limits granted stay length for suspected long-stayers (see visa-legal.md's FMM section), and the 2026 digital-record replacement of the paper FMM gives officers a cleaner repeat-entry trail. Divergence: paper distinguishes tourism from work; practice widely tolerates it, but the tolerance is narrowing, not stable

fact_label: Nature/water adjacency — Chapultepec Park; no coastal or water-body access
value_raw: Bosque de Chapultepec, 866 hectares, largest urban park in Mexico City; city is fully landlocked at 2,240m, no beach/lake/river adjacency
notes: Added 2026-07-19 ([specialist]), closing a zero-fact nature-water-adjacency gap across all five Mexico locations. Decreed a Protected Natural Area in 1992; includes an Aztec-built canal/reservoir/lake system; walkable directly from Roma Norte, Condesa, Polanco, Zona Rosa. Real, substantial urban-nature access, but zero water-body adjacency of any kind — the honest limit against Puerto Vallarta's/Playa del Carmen's direct coastal access

fact_label: Nature/water adjacency — cenotes; Progreso beach 30-45 min away
value_raw: ~2,000 cenotes within 1.5 hours of Mérida; nearest beach (Progreso, Gulf of Mexico) ~30-45 min/48km north
notes: Added 2026-07-19 ([specialist]). No beach in the city itself, but a real day-trip distance, not a beach-town lifestyle; cenotes (Cenote Xlacah/Dzibilchaltún, El Corchito near Progreso) sit under an hour away — a distinctive regional nature feature CDMX/Oaxaca don't have. Beach-distance figure separately sourced: lifeinmerida.com, 'Mérida Mexico & the Beach: Closer Than You Think' (in sources.md's new nature-water-adjacency section)
